candidates.explanation: The refresh flow is meant to rotate the session hash and reject any token whose hash is not the current one. It relies on sessionService.updateByHash({id, hash: data.hash}, {hash}) to do both the check and the rotation. The replay shows the old hash still matches, so that call is not enforcing the old-hash match. I did not see the implementation of updateByHash. It may ignore the hash filter and update by id only, or it may return a session even when nothing matched. refreshToken never compares session.hash with data.hash itself, so a replayed token is accepted and a fresh pair is issued.

validate only checks that sessionId is present. It does not check hash against the stored session, so the guard accepts a rotated token. The only remaining protection is the session lookup in refreshToken.

fix.description: In refreshToken, load the session with sessionService.findById(data.sessionId). Throw UnauthorizedException if it is missing or if session.hash !== data.hash. Only then generate the new hash and call sessionService.update(session.id, { hash }). If updateByHash is kept, make it filter on both id and the old hash and return null when no row matches. Do this atomically, for example with UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND hash = :oldHash, so concurrent replays cannot both succeed.

candidates.explanation: The refresh flow is meant to rotate the session hash and reject any token whose hash is not the current one. It relies on sessionService.updateByHash({id, hash: data.hash}, {hash}) to do both the check and the rotation. The replay shows the old hash still matches, so that call is not enforcing the old-hash match. I did not see the implementation of updateByHash. It may ignore the hash filter and update by id only, or it may return a session even when nothing matched. refreshToken never compares session.hash with data.hash itself, so a replayed token is accepted and a fresh pair is issued.

validate only checks that sessionId is present. It does not check hash against the stored session, so the guard accepts a rotated token. The only remaining protection is the session lookup in refreshToken.

fix.description: In refreshToken, load the session with sessionService.findById(data.sessionId). Throw UnauthorizedException if it is missing or if session.hash !== data.hash. Only then generate the new hash and call sessionService.update(session.id, { hash }). If updateByHash is kept, make it filter on both id and the old hash and return null when no row matches. Do this atomically, for example with UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND hash = :oldHash, so concurrent replays cannot both succeed.
